Population increased in Dorset

The estimated population of Dorset in 2024 was 389,947 usual residents, a rise of 1.0% since 2023.

This meant that Dorset's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Dorset increased by 2.3%.

Over this slightly longer period, Dorset was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Dorset

The average (median) age stayed at 52.2 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Dorset has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Dorset is an area that is classed as intermediate rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Dorset's population of 389,947 usual residents was made up of:

  • 58,061 people aged 0 to 15 years, (14.9%)
  • 212,840 people aged 16 to 64 years, (54.6%)
  • 119,046 people aged 65 years and over, (30.5%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Dorset has a higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (30.5% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Dorset, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Dorset
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Dorset, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 2,658 people (-0.7%). In total, there were 2,512 births and 5,170 deaths in Dorset.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 4,750 (1.2%). There were 21,419 people entering the area and 16,669 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Dorset's population of 1,791 (0.5%) as a result of 2,799 people entering the area and 1,008 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Dorset was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Dorset in mid-2023 is 386,151.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 630 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 712 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 1,342 people.
